title: South Koreans Pick Japan for 'Babymoon' Shopping
paragraphs: It's common for couples who are expecting a child to take a "babymoon" trip. Similar to a honeymoon, it's a way for couples to enjoy one last relaxing holiday before they become parents.
In the past, many South Korean couples chose to have their babymoons in resort destinations like Guam, Bali or Thailand.

However, more and more South Korean couples are now choosing Japan. And instead of choosing a relaxing holiday by a beach in Okinawa, they're traveling to cities like Tokyo and Osaka — because they want to go shopping!
For these couples, their babymoon trips are less about rest and relaxation and more about getting good deals on baby products, like strollers and high chairs.
Because of the weak yen and Japan's tax-free shopping system for foreign visitors, it can be a lot cheaper to buy baby products there than in South Korea.
Japan is also known for having a wide variety of baby products — including many that are hard to find in South Korea.
And of course, Japan is very easy to get to from South Korea.

South Korean babymooners are also sharing stories on social media of their successful shopping trips to Japan, with advice on where to shop, what to buy and how to pack items safely so they don't get damaged on the flight home.
It might not be as restful as a holiday in Guam, but for South Korean couples, a babymoon shopping trip to Japan can mean big savings as they prepare for their new life with a baby.
